templates.createFirst: Create your first message template to get started.
templates.editTitle: Editing triggers Meta re-review — status flips to PENDING.
templates.resubmitTitle: Edit the template and resubmit to Meta for review.
templates.deleteMetaLocallyAria: Delete template from Meta and locally
templates.dialogEditDesc: Save your changes to re-submit to Meta. Status will flip back to PENDING during review.
templates.dialogNewDesc: Build a template and submit it to Meta for approval. Once approved, you can use it in broadcasts and the inbox.
templates.authWarning: AUTHENTICATION templates have a fixed body + OTP button shape that needs a different builder. Create them in Meta WhatsApp Manager for now and use <bold>Sync from Meta</bold> to bring them in.
templates.nameFixed: Name is fixed once a template exists on Meta — create a new template to change it.
templates.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, and underscores only.
templates.langFixed: Language is fixed once a template exists on Meta.
templates.langHint: Must match the exact code on Meta — en_US and en are distinct.
templates.headerSamplePlaceholder: Sample value for {{1}} (required for Meta review)
templates.imageHint: Upload a JPEG/PNG (≤5 MB, ≥800×418 px recommended) or paste a public HTTPS link — we upload it to Meta for review automatically.
templates.mediaHint: Must be a publicly accessible HTTPS link. Meta fetches it once during review, so it needs to stay live for ~24 hrs.
templates.bodyHint: Use {{1}}, {{2}} for variables (must be contiguous starting at {{1}}).
templates.sampleValues: Sample values (Meta uses these to review your template)
templates.buttonsLimit: Up to {max} buttons. QUICK_REPLY buttons must come before URL / phone / copy-code buttons.
templates.urlSamplePlaceholder: Example value for {{1}} (required when URL has a variable)
templates.deleteMetaDesc: "{name}" will be deleted from Meta and from PlastfortSul. Active broadcasts using this template will start failing on their next send. This can't be undone.
templates.deleteLocalDesc: "{name}" will be deleted from PlastfortSul. It was never submitted to Meta, so no remote cleanup is needed.
templates.toastSubmitEditSuccess: Edit submitted — Meta typically reviews within 24 hours.
templates.toastSubmitNewSuccess: Submitted to Meta — typical review time is 24 hours. Status updates automatically.
templates.toastSyncTruncated: Synced the first 2000 templates only — your account has more. Sync again to continue, or contact support if this persists.
templates.toastInvalidImage: Header image must be a JPEG or PNG.
templates.toastImageTooLarge: Image is {size} MB — Meta's limit is 5 MB.

roles.ownerHint: Full control over account and billing

whatsapp.title: WhatsApp connection
whatsapp.description: Connect your Meta WhatsApp Business API. Credentials, webhook, and setup steps all live here.
whatsapp.connectedDesc: Your access token authenticates with Meta. See Registration status below for whether webhooks are actually wired.
whatsapp.notConnectedDesc: Configure your Meta API credentials below to connect your WhatsApp Business account.
whatsapp.registered: Registered — Meta will deliver events to PlastfortSul
whatsapp.notRegistered: Not registered — Meta will not deliver events
whatsapp.subscribedSince: Subscribed since {date}. Click Verify with Meta if events stop arriving.
whatsapp.retryHint: Enter (or correct) the 2-step PIN below and click Save Configuration to retry.
whatsapp.noRegistrationHint: This number was saved before registration tracking existed, or registration was skipped. Enter the 2-step PIN below and click Save Configuration to subscribe it.
whatsapp.apiCredentialsDesc: Enter your Meta WhatsApp Business API credentials.
whatsapp.tokenHidden: Token is hidden for security. Re-enter it to update configuration.
whatsapp.webhookVerifyTokenHint: A custom string you create. Must match the token you set in Meta webhook settings.
whatsapp.pinHint: Needed only to wire inbound messages for a production number. Set it in Meta Business Manager → WhatsApp Accounts → Phone Numbers → Two-step verification, then paste it here so PlastfortSul can subscribe the number — otherwise Meta routes inbound events to whichever app last claimed it (the symptom that hits second numbers under a shared WABA). Meta test numbers have no PIN and are pre-registered — leave this blank for them. Leaving it blank also keeps an existing registration untouched.
whatsapp.webhookDesc: Use this URL as your webhook callback in the Meta App Dashboard.
whatsapp.mediaDesc: Meta deletes received media about 30 days after it arrives. Attachments can be copied to your own storage so they stay viewable.
whatsapp.mirrorInboundDesc: Save a copy of every photo, video, voice note and document customers send. Uses your Supabase storage; files over 16 MB are skipped.
whatsapp.mirrorInboundOffWarning: New attachments will stop being copied and will become unavailable about 30 days after they arrive.
whatsapp.mirrorInboundSaveFailed: Could not update the attachment setting.

whatsapp.step1_4: Fill in app details and create

whatsapp.step2_3: Follow the setup wizard to link your business
whatsapp.step3_3: Copy your WhatsApp Business Account ID
whatsapp.step3_4: Generate a Permanent Access Token from Business Settings > System Users
whatsapp.step4_3: Paste the Webhook Callback URL from above
whatsapp.step4_4: Enter the same Verify Token you set here
whatsapp.toastTokenRequired: Access Token is required for initial setup
whatsapp.toastReenterToken: Please re-enter the Access Token to save changes
whatsapp.toastSavedNoPin: Credentials saved and verified. Inbound registration was skipped (no PIN) — see Registration status below.
whatsapp.toastTestFailed: Connection test failed. Check network and try again.
whatsapp.toastFullyWired: Number is fully wired — Meta is delivering events.
whatsapp.toastNotRegistered: Number is not fully registered. See the checks below for which step failed.
whatsapp.toastVerifyUnreachable: Could not reach the verification endpoint.
whatsapp.toastCleared: Configuration cleared. You can now re-enter your credentials.
whatsapp.toastRegisterFailed: Saved, but Meta couldn't register the number: {reason}
whatsapp.resetConfirm: This deletes the current WhatsApp configuration so you can enter it again. Continue?
whatsapp.toggleTokenVisibility: Show or hide the access token

profile.title: Your profile
profile.description: How you show up across the app. Your avatar and name appear in the header, sidebar, and anywhere your teammates see you.
profile.photoHint: PNG, JPG, WebP, or GIF. Up to 2 MB.
profile.emailChangeHint: Check the inbox for <bold>{oldEmail}</bold> and <bold>{newEmail}</bold> — both need to confirm before the change takes effect.
profile.userIdCopyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select and copy it by hand.
profile.unsupportedImageDesc: Use PNG, JPG, WebP, or GIF.
profile.profileSavedEmailCheck: Profile saved — check your email to confirm the address change
profile.passwordDesc: Use at least {min} characters. You will stay signed in on this device after changing it.
profile.cannotChangeNoEmail: Cannot change password without a current email
profile.passwordTooShort: Password must be at least {min} characters
profile.passwordMismatch: New password and confirmation do not match
profile.sessionsDesc: Sign out of every device where you're logged in — including this one. Useful if you lost a laptop or shared your password.
profile.signOutConfirmDesc: Every device logged into this account will be signed out and will need to log in again. You will be redirected to the login page.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Set the mode and accent colour used across the app. Saved to this device — try it, it changes live.

plastfortsul.tagline: The brand — a blue that marks where you are, not what is urgent.

emerald.tagline: Growth-coded, nods at messaging without copying WhatsApp green.

cobalt.tagline: Clean B2B-SaaS blue — calm and product-y.

amber.tagline: Warm and friendly — feels good for SMB teams.

rose.tagline: Bold and modern — D2C, creator-economy, lifestyle.

install.title: Install on this device
install.promptBody: Install the CRM as an app: it opens full screen, with no browser bar, and gets its own icon on your home screen.
install.iosBody: On iPhone, Safari does this itself. Once added, the CRM opens full screen with no browser bar.
install.installedBody: You are already running the CRM as an app — that is why there is no browser bar here.

security.title: Login & security
security.description: Change your password and sign out of your devices. These keep your account safe.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.description: Keys authenticate the public REST API (<apiCode>/api/v1</apiCode>) so you can build your own automations. Send them as <headerCode>Authorization: Bearer <key></headerCode>.
apiKeys.createOneHint: Click <bold>New API key</bold> to create one.
apiKeys.askAdminHint: Ask an admin to create one.
apiKeys.scopesHint: A key with no scopes can still call GET /api/v1/me to verify it works.
apiKeys.copyDesc: This is the only time the full key is shown. Store it somewhere safe — if you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
apiKeys.copyFailed: Copy failed — select and copy manually
apiKeys.newKeyDesc: Name it after the integration that will use it, and grant only the scopes it needs.

scopes.messagesRead: Read messages and their delivery status
scopes.webhooksManage: Register and manage outbound event webhooks
scopes.fieldsRead: Read custom field definitions (name, type and the id automations use)
scopes.dealsWrite: Create a deal and move it between stages

deals.title: Deals & currency
deals.description: The currency used for new deals and for pipeline and dashboard totals.
deals.defaultCurrencyDesc: New deals default to this currency, and pipeline and dashboard totals are shown in it. Existing deals keep the currency they were saved with.
deals.adminOnlyHint: Only account admins can change the default currency.

aiConfig.title: Agent setup
aiConfig.description: Bring your own OpenAI or Anthropic key. PlastfortSul calls the provider directly with your key — no per-seat AI fees, and your data stays yours. This powers AI-drafted replies in the inbox, the auto-reply bot, and the Playground.
aiConfig.adminOnlyConfig: Only admins and owners can change the AI configuration.
aiConfig.encryptionNotice: Your key is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never shown again after saving.
aiConfig.embeddingsHint: An OpenAI key used only to embed your knowledge base (text-embedding-3-small){sameKeyText}. Leave blank to use keyword search instead. Clear it to turn semantic search off.
aiConfig.sameKeyText: — can be the same key as above
aiConfig.behaviourDesc: Tell the assistant about your business — products, tone, what it may and may not promise. This context feeds both drafts and auto-replies.
aiConfig.promptPlaceholder: e.g. We are Acme, a coffee-equipment store. Be warm and concise. Never quote prices or delivery dates — hand off to a human for those.
aiConfig.enableAssistantDesc: Master switch. Turns on the “Draft with AI” button in the inbox.
aiConfig.autoReplyDesc: The bot answers new inbound messages automatically (only when no flow handles them and no agent is assigned). Hands off to a human when it can’t help.
aiConfig.maxAutoRepliesDesc: After this many bot replies in one thread, the bot goes quiet.
aiConfig.handoffToDesc: When the bot can’t help — or hits the reply cap — it pauses and routes the chat here, with a short note on what happened.
aiConfig.handoffQueue: Unassigned queue (any agent can pick it up)
aiConfig.toggleKeyVisibility: Show or hide the API key
aiConfig.mediaUnderstandingDesc: Every voice note and photo a customer sends is turned into text on arrival, on your own key. Without it those messages reach the inbox with no words in them — nothing to search, no keyword to trigger on.

aiKnowledge.title: Knowledge base
aiKnowledge.description: Add FAQs, policies, or product details. The assistant retrieves the relevant pieces when drafting and auto-replying, so it can answer instead of handing off.{searchType}
aiKnowledge.semanticSearchOn: Semantic search is on (embeddings key set).
aiKnowledge.keywordSearchOn: Using keyword search — add an embeddings key above for semantic search.
aiKnowledge.editDocContentPlaceholder: Paste the FAQ answer, policy text, or product details…
aiKnowledge.reindexTooltip: Re-embed all documents (e.g. after adding an embeddings key)

aiAgent.description: Your bring-your-own-key AI agent — set it up, then test it in the playground before it replies to customers in the inbox.
aiAgent.title: AI agent

quickReplies.title: Quick replies
quickReplies.description: Reusable snippets — text, a file or a saved interactive message — that agents insert from the inbox composer by typing /.
quickReplies.empty: No quick replies yet. Create one to reuse it across conversations.
quickReplies.shortcutHint: Optional. In the chat, type / followed by the shortcut to insert this reply.
quickReplies.captionPlaceholder: Caption to send with the file (optional)
quickReplies.mediaPick: Choose a photo, video or document
quickReplies.mediaHint: The file is sent with the message. Agents can still edit the caption before sending.
quickReplies.mediaRequired: Choose a file for this quick reply.
quickReplies.nameRequired: Give the quick reply a name.
quickReplies.needsMigration: Shortcuts and file snippets are waiting on migration 044. Text and interactive quick replies still work.

aiPlayground.emptyState: Send a message to see how your agent would reply.
aiPlayground.title: Playground
aiPlayground.subtitle: — test replies as if you were a customer
aiPlayground.emptyHint: It uses your knowledge base and behaves exactly like the auto-reply bot — including handoff.
aiPlayground.goToSetup: Not set up yet? Go to Setup
aiPlayground.notConfigured: No agent configured yet — finish Setup first.
aiPlayground.wouldHandOff: Would hand off to a human here

aiUsage.title: Token usage
aiUsage.description: Tokens spent on your provider key by drafts and the auto-reply bot. Counts only — no message content is stored here.
aiUsage.emptyTitle: No AI usage in the last {days} days yet.
aiUsage.emptyBody: This fills in as the assistant drafts and auto-replies.
aiUsage.modelSummary: {tokens} tok · {calls, plural, one {# call} other {# calls}}
aiUsage.truncated: Showing a partial window — usage is high enough that only the most recent records are summarized here.

access.title: Access & audit
access.description: What each person may do, and a record of what has already been done to this account.
access.restrictedBody: This page shows every member's sign-in times and every change made to the account.
access.permissionsSub: The role is the base. Here you write the exceptions for one person.
access.scopeNote: These exceptions are applied by the interface and by this app. They change what a person sees and can do here — they are not a database-level lock. Where that difference matters, change the role instead.
access.noEditableBody: Exceptions are written for other people — not for the owner, and not for yourself. Invite a colleague first.
access.pickMember: Pick somebody above to see what they can do.
access.overridden: Exception for this person · the {role} role says {roleAnswer}
access.denyOnly: can only be taken away, never granted above the role
access.resetToRole: Back to what the role says
access.auditSub: Who did what, and when. Nobody can edit or delete a line here.
access.auditFailed: Could not load the audit log
access.auditPendingBody: The audit log is ready in the app — it is waiting for the table to be created in the database.
access.auditEmptyBody: Sign-ins, role changes, keys and integration settings all land here as they happen.

caps.productsViewDesc: A price somebody cannot look up is a price they ask a colleague for.

assignment.title: Automatic assignment
assignment.description: Who gets the next conversation, and by what rule. Nothing here ever takes a thread away from somebody already handling it.
assignment.pendingBody: The rules below are ready in the app. Until the migration runs, only the strategy can be saved — the rest keeps the behaviour it has today.
assignment.strategyTitle: How the next one is picked
assignment.strategySub: Applies only to conversations that have no owner yet.
assignment.modeOffBody: New conversations stay unassigned until somebody picks them up.
assignment.modeRoundRobinBody: Round the team in order, resuming after whoever got the last one. Fair by turn — it does not look at how much work anybody already has.
assignment.modeLeastBusyBody: Whoever holds the fewest open conversations right now. Ties fall back to taking turns, so a quiet morning still spreads out.
assignment.rulesSub: Who is eligible, and what happens at the edges.
assignment.rulesOff: Turn a strategy on above to use these.
assignment.minRoleDesc: A reader cannot reply, so assigning to one hides a waiting customer behind an owner who is unable to act. Agent and up is the sensible floor.
assignment.fallbackDesc: Out of hours the choice is an owner who sees it in the morning, or no owner at all. Which is better depends on whether your team watches the unassigned tab.
assignment.maxOpenDesc: Skip somebody already holding this many open conversations. 0 means no ceiling. Ignored when everybody is at it — a cap that can jam the queue is worse than no cap.
assignment.needsMigration: Migration 051 has not been applied yet.
assignment.rosterSub: Anybody can take themselves out. Admins can take anybody out — for the owner who does sales and not support.
assignment.rosterEmptyBody: Invite a colleague and they show up here.
assignment.modeBestScoreBody: Sends to whoever replies fastest and resolves most, computed over the last 30 days. Ties go into the rotation, and somebody with no history yet counts as mid-table — otherwise they would never get the conversation that would give them one.
assignment.reassignTitle: Hand over when the owner is away
assignment.reassignDesc: If a customer has been waiting longer than this AND whoever holds the conversation has not been seen in the same period, it passes to somebody available. Never to another absent person.
assignment.reassignWarning: On: a conversation waiting {minutes} min with an absent owner changes hands on its own. Who had it, who received it and how long the customer waited are all recorded.

rooms.title: Team rooms
rooms.description: Name the room you already have, say what it is for, and make another one when the team needs to keep two conversations apart.
rooms.pendingBody: Rooms are ready in the app — they are waiting for the table to be created in the database. Until then there is the one room, and it works.
rooms.newRoomSub: Everybody in the account can read and write every room. These are folders, not private channels.
rooms.name: Name
rooms.descriptionHint: A room with no description is a room three people will each use for something different.
rooms.listSub: The first one is the room this account started with. It can be renamed, and it cannot be removed.
rooms.archivedSub: Out of the switcher, not deleted. Everything said in them is still there and comes back with the room.
rooms.archiveConfirm: Archive this room? It leaves the switcher; nothing said in it is deleted.
rooms.defaultNameHint: Leave it empty and this room goes back to being called "{name}".

aiWizard.stepKeySummary: The assistant runs on your own provider account. Nothing is billed through this CRM.
aiWizard.apiKeyDesc: Stored encrypted. Nobody in this CRM can read it back — replace it if you lose it.
aiWizard.stepPersonaSummary: The name it answers by, what this business does, and how it should sound. This is where most wrong answers get fixed.
aiWizard.personaPlaceholder: e.g. Ana, from the front desk
aiWizard.businessDesc: The single most valuable line on this page. Most wrong answers are a model that does not know what business it is in.
aiWizard.businessPlaceholder: We are a packaging distributor in Caxias do Sul. We sell bin bags, stretch film and boxes to condominiums, shops and small factories.
aiWizard.extraPrompt: Anything else it should always know
aiWizard.extraPromptDesc: Free text, appended to everything above. Opening hours, delivery areas, the way you refer to your own products.
aiWizard.stepKnowledgeSummary: Your own documents. The assistant reads the passages relevant to each question instead of being told everything at once.
aiWizard.embeddingsKeyDesc: An OpenAI key. With it, the assistant finds a passage that answers the question even when it uses different words. Without it, search falls back to matching words.
aiWizard.retrievalTopKDesc: 0 turns retrieval off, which is useful while tuning a prompt. Pinned documents are always included and do not count here.
aiWizard.stepToolsSummary: Lookups the assistant can run mid-sentence, in this account only, about this customer only.
aiWizard.toolsNote: Every lookup here is read-only. The assistant cannot tag, move, create or send anything — those stay with people.
aiWizard.stepLimitsSummary: What it must never do, and when it should fetch a person instead of answering.
aiWizard.guardrailsDesc: One per line. These are read last, which is what makes a model honour them.
aiWizard.guardrailsPlaceholder:
Never quote a delivery date.
Never offer a discount.
Never say a product is in stock.
aiWizard.escalationDesc: Only used while replying automatically. One per line.
aiWizard.escalationPlaceholder:
The customer is complaining.
The customer asks for a quote above R$ 5,000.
The customer asks to speak to somebody.
aiWizard.autoReplyDesc: With nobody watching. Off means it only ever suggests, and a person sends.
aiWizard.handoffQueue: Nobody — leave it in the queue
aiWizard.stepLiveSummary: The master switch, and the two places the assistant helps without answering a customer.
aiWizard.isActiveDesc: Nothing below works while this is off.
aiWizard.assistDesc: A button on a customer message that drafts an answer for a person to edit. Nothing is sent by itself.
aiWizard.mediaDesc: Every voice note and photo becomes text on arrival, so it can be searched and matched.
aiWizard.toolsMoved: Suggested replies, audio transcription and image/document reading moved out of here. They never talk to a customer, and they now live under <link>AI tools</link> — so turning the agent off no longer turns them off with it.

agentLookups.getContactDesc: Name, company, city, last purchase, average ticket.
agentLookups.getOpenDealDesc: Title, stage, value and expected close date, when there is one.
agentLookups.searchProductsDesc: Name, code, price and unit. Needs the catalogue to exist.
agentLookups.searchKnowledgeDesc: For things the passages already in front of it do not cover.

aiTools.title: AI tools
aiTools.description: The AI a PERSON operates: suggest a reply, transcribe an audio, read an image or a PDF. None of them talks to a customer — which is why they are configured apart from the AI agent.
aiTools.noKey: These functions use the same provider key as the agent. <link>Add the key under AI agent</link> to turn them on.
aiTools.masterDesc: Independent of the AI agent. You can keep the bot off and still have audio transcribed and replies suggested.
aiTools.functionsDesc: One switch per function, because what each one costs is very different.
aiTools.suggestDesc: An agent asks for a suggestion on a customer message. The text lands in the composer to be edited — nothing is sent on its own.
aiTools.audioDesc: Writes down what was said in an inbound voice note. It is what lets search, keyword triggers and the conversation preview see something where they see nothing today.
aiTools.imageDesc: Describes an inbound photo and transcribes any invoice number, amount or plate visible in it, word for word.
aiTools.documentDesc: Summarises orders, invoices and price tables sent as PDFs. Off by default: the most expensive of the three, and a file can arrive twenty pages long unannounced.
aiTools.modelDesc: Optional. The agent answers everybody all day and wants something cheap; this runs when somebody asks, and can be worth something better.
aiTools.saveFailed: Could not save the AI tools.
aiTools.audioNeedsOpenAi: Anthropic cannot hear. On this account transcription uses the OpenAI embeddings key — <link>add it under AI agent</link>, or audio will arrive and nothing will happen.

hooks.title: Inbound webhooks
hooks.description: A URL Typebot, n8n or a landing page can call to hand data to the CRM. What arrives becomes {{vars.field}} inside automations.
hooks.pendingHint: The screen is ready in the app — it is waiting for the tables to be created in the database.
hooks.newDesc: The URL is generated now and shown exactly once.
hooks.ipsHint: Comma separated. Empty accepts from anywhere. If your n8n and Typebot run on your own server this is the cheapest lock there is — it changes nothing at the sending end. It does not protect against a loop in your own flow; the 60-per-minute ceiling does.
hooks.messagesDesc: Without this, the webhook only writes to the CRM: fields, tags and deals.
hooks.messagesWarning: Turn this on only if you need it. With it on, anybody holding the URL — or a loop in your flow — can make the company's number send WhatsApp messages, and that is how a number gets banned by Meta.
hooks.tokenOnce: Copy it now. It is not stored in plaintext and cannot be shown again — if you lose it, create another.
hooks.revokeConfirmDesc: The URL stops working immediately and cannot be recovered. This webhook's delivery history is deleted too.
hooks.noDeliveriesHint: As soon as Typebot or n8n call this URL, what arrived shows up here — with the automation that ran and where it stopped.
hooks.nothingRanHint: The data arrived fine. What is missing is an automation with the "Webhook received" trigger — or the ones that exist did not pass their conditions.
hooks.varsHint: In automations each field above is a variable; a nested field becomes name.of.field.

Notifications.title: Notifications
Notifications.description: New customer messages and conversations your teammates assign to you show up here.
Notifications.emptyDesc: You'll see an alert here when a customer writes or someone assigns you a conversation.
Notifications.toastFailedMarkRead: Failed to mark notification as read
Notifications.toastFailedMarkAll: Failed to mark all as read

Routes.notFoundBody: This address doesn't exist, or it stopped existing. Check the link, or go back to where the work is.
Routes.errorBody: The rest of the app is still running. Try again — if it happens a second time, send the code below along.
Routes.fatalBody: Reload the page. If it fails again, the problem is on our side.

notFound.title: Invite not found
notFound.body: This link doesn’t match a valid invitation. Double-check the URL or ask the person who invited you to send a new one.

used.title: Invite already used
used.body: This invitation has already been accepted. If that wasn’t you, ask the account admin to send a fresh link.

expired.title: Invite expired
expired.body: This invitation has expired. Ask the account admin to send a new one — they take a few seconds to generate.

serverError.title: Something went wrong
serverError.body: We couldn’t verify this invitation right now. Try refreshing the page in a moment.

Join.joinAs: You’ll join as <role></role>. Link valid until {date}.
Join.acceptNote: Accepting moves your login into <account></account>. Your empty personal account from signup will be cleaned up.
Join.conflictFallback: You are already in another account. Sign in with a different email to join this one.
Join.conflictBody: To join <account></account>, sign out and sign up again with a different email address. The invite link stays valid as long as it hasn’t expired.
Join.signOutDifferentEmail: Sign out & use a different email
Join.toastSignOutFailed: Could not sign out. Try refreshing the page.

waiting.title: Waiting looks after itself
waiting.body: The customer writes and the thread moves to Waiting; somebody answers and it returns to Inbox. Nobody has to mark anything, and the tab sorts oldest first so the forgotten one surfaces.

teamRoom.title: The team has a room
teamRoom.body: An internal conversation inside the CRM, so the note about a case sits next to the case. Nothing written there reaches a customer.

conversationMenu.title: Act without opening the thread
conversationMenu.body: Right-click any row in the list, or the menu on a phone, to mark as waiting, finish, assign, hide or delete.

firstRelease.title: The first release
firstRelease.body: WhatsApp inbox, contacts, pipelines, campaigns and automations.

weekStrip.title: The week at the top of the screen
weekStrip.body: Seven days beside the search, with a dot on any day that has something on it — a deal closing, a repurchase, an occurrence, an automation, a campaign or a birthday. Click a day to see what it is, from any screen.

assignFromList.title: Assign without opening the conversation
assignFromList.body: Right-click a conversation and pick the owner there. “Nobody” puts it back in the automatic rotation.

mediaThumb.title: The conversation row shows the right media
mediaThumb.body: A photo with a caption now shows both, and an automated reply stopped inheriting the photo the customer had sent earlier.

customColors.title: The colour is yours
customColors.body: Tags and pipeline stages take any colour, not the six on a list — pick it in the system picker or type the code. The preview shows how the chip will read before you save.

audioToText.title: Audio becomes text
audioToText.body: Every voice note and image a customer sends gets a written description — it shows in the conversation preview, joins the search, and makes keyword automations work. It can be switched off in the AI settings.

products.title: Products, and a deal that adds itself up
products.body: A catalogue with prices and codes. Pick the items inside a deal and the value calculates itself; what a customer is interested in stays on their record and becomes a campaign audience.

aiAssist.title: AI helps you answer
aiAssist.body: Right-click a customer message: summarise, translate, suggest a reply, or adjust the tone of what you wrote. Without leaving the conversation.

teamMedia.title: Screenshots, video and audio in the team room
teamMedia.body: Drag, paste with Ctrl+V, or record audio in the browser. Files sit in a private bucket — only account members can read them, and none of it reaches a customer.

playbookConsult.title: Playbook, in the menu
playbookConsult.body: Sales scripts, objections, operating rules and product sheets, in one search. The pipeline checklist is now called Stage steps.

quieterUi.title: The product stopped shouting
quieterUi.body: Reports and Overview use a neutral surface: tone lives in the icon and the figure, not in the card background.

funnelFlow.title: The sales funnel runs on its own
funnelFlow.body: Ten ready-made models: /aberto, 24 h without a reply, the follow-up sequence, the fridge, /andamento, /atendido, after-sale and repurchase, future purchase and birthday. Install, check the stages, activate.

replyCancels.title: Whoever replies leaves the queue
replyCancels.body: A customer reply cancels pending waits and moves the deal to Em Negociação. Nobody switches anything off by hand.

shortcutsMove.title: /aberto, /andamento and /atendido move the deal
shortcutsMove.body: The quick reply you use in the inbox becomes a trigger. The CRM records which shortcut went out and moves the stage for you.

items.waitingTab: Waiting means the customer is waiting for a reply: a thread lands there when they write and leaves when somebody answers.
items.messageNotifications: A new customer message rings the bell. Only assignment did before.
items.contactName: An edited contact name no longer reverts.
items.occurrenceWarning: A registered occurrence shows on the contact, with the count in the panel.
items.signupButton: The create-account button no longer overflows the edge.
items.teamRoom: My team: an internal conversation, inside the CRM.
items.conversationMenu: Right-click a conversation (or the menu on a phone) to mark, finish and assign.
items.hideConversation: Hide a conversation: it leaves the list without deleting, and returns if the customer writes.
items.autoAssign: Automatic round-robin assignment among whoever is online.
items.contactPhoto: Contact profile photos on the contact form.
items.pasteImage: Ctrl+V pastes a screenshot into the message field. Dragging a file works too.
items.mediaPreview: Audio, photos and documents show an icon and a name instead of [audio].
items.signature: A signed message no longer shows the name in asterisks.
items.mobileThread: The conversation on a phone: header and field fit the screen, and the keyboard capitalises again.
items.phoneMask: Phone numbers are masked: +55 (51) 99000-0001 instead of a run of digits.
items.inviteScreen: The invitation screen uses the same design as the sign-in screens.
items.agendaEmpty: Agenda: the "nothing scheduled" state is centred beside the calendar.
items.editorCanvas: Flows and automations are drawn on the same grid, edge to edge.
items.firstRelease: First release: shared inbox, contacts, pipelines, campaigns and automations.
items.playbook: The commercial playbook, inside the CRM.
items.uxOverhaul: General interface pass: menus, notifications, the calendar and spacing.
items.onlineMembers: Who is online shows in the header, on every screen.
items.teamPreview: The team's last message shows in the sidebar, from any page.
items.presenceLocale: Presence timestamps in the app language — they were English.
items.weekStrip: The week shows beside the search, with a dot on any day that has something on it.
items.assignFromList: You can pick the owner by right-clicking a conversation.
items.onlineFaces: Who is online reads from the faces, each carrying its own presence dot.
items.mediaThumb: A captioned photo shows both; a flow or automation reply no longer inherits the previous media.
items.closedFilter: The Closed and Hidden filters work again — they were permanently disabled.
items.contactNameAgain: A name edited from the contact page no longer reverts to the WhatsApp one.
items.csvNames: Imported CSV names stop being overwritten too.
items.waitingClock: Parking an already-waiting conversation no longer resets its place in the queue.
items.phoneMaskSecond: The phone field on the contact page got the mask and saves in the canonical format.
items.foreignPhone: A foreign number shows the correct country code.
items.teamRoomExit: You can leave the team room on a phone.
items.teamRoomDot: The team room unread dot clears once you have read it.
items.teamRoomLink: The team room shortcut works on every click, not only the first.
items.notificationRead: Marking a notification read reports a failure instead of pretending.
items.notificationDeadClick: A notification with nowhere to go no longer looks like a broken button.
items.emptyFlowCanvas: A brand-new flow opens on the same grid as one that has nodes.
items.translations: Over thirty screens and messages that were still in English were translated.
items.customColors: Tags and pipeline stages take any colour, with a preview of how the chip will read.
items.audioToText: Customer audio and images become text — in the preview, in search, and in keyword automations.
items.products: A product catalogue, with deal items that add the value up on their own.
items.aiAssist: AI help on the customer message: summarise, translate, suggest a reply, adjust the tone.
items.accountAudit: Account audit: who changed what, and each person last sign-in.
items.memberPermissions: Permissions per person, on top of the role. The owner never loses access.
items.assignScore: Assignment by best performance, and automatic handover when an agent does not reply.
items.teamRoomNames: Team rooms with a name and description, and messages you can edit and delete.
items.inboundHooks: An inbound webhook for Typebot and n8n, with a token, scopes and a deliveries screen.
items.installApp: The CRM can be installed on a phone as an app.
items.cnpjCheck: CNPJ checked on the form, with a warning when the customer already exists.
items.aiAgentDepth: AI agent with a persona, tone, escalation rules, tools and a knowledge base.
items.reportsRedesign: Reports redesigned: funnel, free date range, and a comparison with the previous period.
items.settingsOneArea: Admin and Settings became one area, showing the sections your role opens.
items.profilePhotos: Your profile photo shows in the team, in the conversation and in the sidebar.
items.mobileNav: On a phone the navigation moved down to the thumb, and the conversation list responds to a swipe.
items.messageAuthor: A reply shows who answered, and the delivery tick like WhatsApp.
items.productDialogs: The browser grey boxes became product dialogs.
items.periodCompare: The comparison with the previous period miscounted above a thousand conversations.
items.teamMedia: Team room: screenshots, video, audio, drag, paste and record. The file stays private.
items.playbookConsult: Playbook in the menu: scripts, objections, rules and product sheets. One search covers all four.
items.sendCost: Send cost in Reports: what went out, what Meta billed, and which category — no money amounts.
items.reportsCharts: Three new charts: grouped conversation bars, a three-column funnel, response time as multiples of the target.
items.dashboardLayout: Overview: the four alerts became rows, the agenda moved beside them, and “What the CRM did today” sits with its counterpart again.
items.controlBorders: Field borders are light; checkboxes and radios still meet 3:1 contrast.
items.profileAvatar: The profile photo shows on the CRM card and in the conversation header — both used to show initials only.
items.settingsSticky: The Settings rail no longer scrolls away with the page.
items.reportsSkeleton: The Reports loading state matches the page, not the old four-box strip.
items.funnelFlow: Ten sales-funnel models under Automations, resolving stages, tags and shortcuts by name on install.
items.dealStageTrigger: “Deal entered a stage” trigger — from the board, the thread, the API or another automation.
items.teamMessageTrigger: “Message sent by the team” trigger, by quick reply or by template.
items.dateTrigger: “Contact date is today” trigger: the birthday, once per contact per day.
items.dealSteps: Steps to move and update the deal, cancel other automations and end the run.
items.waitUntilDate: A wait until the future-purchase date, which follows the date if it is moved on the agenda.
items.replyCancels: Per-automation rules: cancel when the customer replies or when the deal enters chosen stages.
items.reentryRules: A reentry policy, and never two runs at once for the same deal.
items.logsReasons: The history shows the deal and why the run ended; cancelled and skipped became statuses.
items.lossReasons: Loss reasons are the eight of the official flow; “Stopped replying” left the list.
items.wonStage: Em Andamento is now the sale and asks for the value on entry; Venda Perdida asks for the reason.
items.deadTriggersHidden: Triggers that never fired (Schedule, Conversation assigned) left the menu.

Products.title: Products
Products.description: What you sell, with a code and a price. Line items on an opportunity come from here, and so do the answers the assistant gives about price.
Products.pendingBody: The catalogue is ready in the app — it is waiting for the table to be created in the database. Until then an opportunity keeps its typed value.
Products.formSub: Only the name is required. Everything else can be filled in later.
Products.name: Name
Products.skuPlaceholder: the one already printed on the box
Products.categoryDesc: What this belongs with. It is what makes “campaign by product” a filter rather than a naming convention everybody has to remember.
Products.descriptionHint: Measurements, thickness, how many per box. The assistant reads this when the catalogue lookup is on — it is the difference between “yes, we have it” and an answer with the numbers in it.
Products.duplicateSku: That code is already on another product. Two rows with one code means the price you quote depends on which one the query found.
Products.emptyBody: Add the ten things you sell most. That is enough for quotes to start adding themselves up.
Products.noMatchBody: Try part of the name, or the code.
Products.dimensionsHint: Typed, not written into the description — it is what makes “all the 40x60” a search instead of a paragraph somebody has to read.
Products.adminOnly: Only an admin can create or retire a product. Correcting one is yours.

Playbook.title: Playbook
Playbook.description: What to say, and what the company agreed on. To check mid-conversation.
Playbook.variablesHint: Use [Name], [Company], [Product], [Value] as a reminder of what to swap. The text is copied as written.
Playbook.emptyHint: Whatever is written here is available to the whole team during a conversation.
Playbook.missingBody: It needs migration 064. Ask whoever runs the database.
Playbook.emptyProducts: Products added under Products show up here for reference.
